rules.statement: For every form-bound POST endpoint protected by antiforgery, add an integration test that posts the form without the antiforgery token and asserts a 4xx response and that no state changed (session still valid, any pending operation still unspent).
rules.why: Test helpers that always add the token hide a route where antiforgery isn't enforced or a missing token fails with a 500, letting a cross-site post change state undetected.
rules.check: A diff adding or changing a form-bound POST endpoint with no accompanying test that omits the antiforgery token and checks both the 4xx status and that the side effects did not happen.

rules.statement: Make a security-relevant flag on a result type that replaceable handlers construct a required (positional or `required`) member, or have it default to the safe value, instead of an optional `init` property that defaults to the unsafe value.
rules.why: A custom handler built on the existing constructor silently leaves the flag at its default and fails open, with no compile-time or runtime signal.
rules.check: New bool or enum members on public records or DTOs returned by extensibility points (commands, providers) that control a security check and default to the permissive value through an optional `init` property.

rules.statement: Log a distinct, named event before returning an error for a security-relevant rejection, such as a session or binding mismatch, and keep session ids, tokens and continuation state out of the log message.
rules.why: Without a distinct event, operators can't tell an attack attempt from an ordinary stale or invalid request. Comparable rejections nearby already log.
rules.check: New rejection branches (400/403 returns) for security checks that log nothing, or that reuse a generic event, or whose log arguments include session ids, tokens or state payloads.
